failure_summary.description: Follow-ups re-searched or filtered from an unsuitable cached result instead of applying only the new constraint to the suitable cached base.
Requested result-producing work was omitted or its tool result was not assigned and saved to cache.
An explicit non-stop flight request was not mapped to zero layovers.
An arrival requested by a stated time was mapped to a lower bound rather than an upper bound.
The agent asked for missing inputs for some domains but failed to search a separately requested domain whose inputs were available.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly covers assigning and caching tool results and updating suitable cached results, so repeating those rules would not patch a content gap. These edits clarify two missing flight-language mappings and make the existing independent-domain requirement operational by requiring ready searches and missing-input questions to be handled together.

edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.
edits.content: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X,” “by X,” or “no later than X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`; “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`. Preserve the stated AM/PM value.
- **Map direct flights explicitly:** For a request for a “non-stop,” “nonstop,” or “direct” flight, set `num_layovers=[0]` in each applicable flight search.

edits.target: Check required inputs independently by domain: seek missing information, but proceed with other requested searches whose inputs are available.
edits.content: Check required inputs independently for each requested domain: in the same generated code, execute and cache every search whose required inputs are available, and use `seek_information` only for missing required inputs in the other domains. Do not block ready searches or ask again for information already established in the conversation.
